subject: BrightLane onboarding: access controls (SSO/SCIM, IP allowlist, service accounts)
messages:
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@brightlane.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: it-admin@brightlane.com
Date: 2028-03-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BrightLane onboarding: access controls and network constraints

Hi Markus / Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick follow-up. We're ready to kick off the access controls portion of our onboarding. High-level items we need covered in the next 2 weeks:

- SSO / SAML integration (IdP: Okta) — we need guidance on metadata, ACS urls, and certificate rollover windows.
- SCIM provisioning (group sync for product access) — limited to a handful of groups at launch.
- IP allowlist — production egress is restricted to a small set of static ranges; we'll need to provide those and request maintenance windows for testing.
- Service accounts & keys — we require short-lived credentials and audit trails; permanent keys require justification.
- Org policies & tagging — we need RBAC boundaries for prod vs non-prod.
- Evidence & reports — SOC2 attestation and audit log retention details for procurement.

I've attached our security requirements doc and the IdP metadata (separate message). Can you confirm a proposed technical kickoff time and what prework you need from BrightLane?

Attachments: [attachment: BrightLane_Security_Reqs.pdf]

Thanks,
Tara Singh
Head of IT, BrightLane
T: +1 415 555 0198

- Introductions & roles (5 min)
- SAML metadata exchange and verify ACS/cert details (10 min)
- SCIM scope & provisioning cadence (5 min)
- IP allowlist testing window and egress ranges (5 min)
- Service account model (ephemeral vs long-lived) + audit logging (10 min)
- Action items & mutual action plan link (5 min)

Prework for BrightLane:
1) Provide Okta metadata file or endpoint (xml).
2) List of IP ranges for allowlist and a proposed test window (UTC preferred).
3) Pilot user group names for SCIM sync.
4) Any procurement evidence (SOC2 pdf) you want us to reference.

I'm attaching our internal onboarding checklist so you can see our typical deliverables. Proposed kickoff: today 2:30 PM PT or tomorrow 10:00 AM PT — which works for you?

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: 2028-03-01T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BrightLane onboarding: access controls and network constraints

Tara / team — looping in the security engineering perspective. A few clarifications and proposals:

1) SAML/Certs — we'll consume the metadata URL and test against a non-prod SP consumer first. Cert rollover: we can support two active certs for a rolling rotation. Suggested TTL for SAML assertion validation is 5 minutes.

2) SCIM provisioning — we'll implement incremental provisioning for the initial groups and run a dry-run that logs but does not apply changes. We'll request SCIM write scope limited to the three group handles you provided. Canary plan: add 2 test users to BH-Admins in staging and validate access mapping before broad sync.

3) Service accounts — recommended model: short-lived service tokens issued by Redwood's ephemeral credential broker with 12-hour TTL by default; for integrations that cannot accept that, we can issue HSM-wrapped long-lived keys with rotation policy and audit hooks.

4) IP allowlist — we'll provide a test endpoint and request that your firewall team open egress for our test IPs during the window Tara suggested. Please confirm whether NATting will change source IPs for outbound traffic; if so, share post-NAT ranges.

5) Audit logs & retention — we can surface tenant-level audit logs to BrightLane for 24 months; for longer retention we can provide S3 export configuration. Will need a PO line for extended retention if you want us to manage it beyond standard SLA.

Action items for BrightLane: confirm NAT behavior, firewall ticket updates (FL-8819), and identify two staging users for the canary.

—Ben Carter
Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
